# Standard work audit

Whether a work instruction is actually being followed weeks after it was written — the sustainment audit's shape, applied to standard work instead of a kaizen event.

Family: Standard work · Format: .xlsx · Domain: core

## What it is

A work instruction written once and never checked again tends to drift from what people actually do. This audit is the sustainment audit's exact shape, applied to a work instruction: restate what it was supposed to ensure, get a checklist of specific practices to verify, and see honestly which are still holding weeks or months later.

## When to use it

Use it when:

- A work instruction has been in place long enough to check whether it's actually still followed, not just written.
- You want to catch instruction drift — the real practice diverging from the documented one — before it becomes the norm.
- You want to close a gap the instruction itself flagged when it was first built (a missing key point, an unclear step).

Not when:

- The instruction was just written — give it real time to settle before auditing it.

## How to fill it in

- **originalObjective** — What was the work instruction supposed to ensure?
- **checks** — Drafted from what the instruction was supposed to change — verify what's actually still holding.
- **narrative** — Drafted from the checklist actually built.

## What good looks like

The example below audits the tier-3 work instruction for triaging renewal-risk tickets, fifty-one days after it was written — including whether the step it originally flagged with no key point still has that gap.

Full worked example, on-screen and as a downloadable .xlsx: https://www.katafacts.com/katas/standard-work-audit

## Common mistakes

- **Auditing an instruction that was never actually rolled out.** — A sustainment audit checks whether real practice has drifted from a real standard — there's nothing to check if the standard was never actually used.
- **Marking a practice as holding without actually verifying it on the floor.** — The audit only has value if it reflects reality, not a hopeful assumption.

## What it connects to

Upstream:

- **Work instruction** — The instruction's own steps and key points are exactly what this audit checks against reality.

## Where AI helps

Judgement — stays with you:

- Deciding how much time to give an instruction before auditing it
- Deciding what to do about a practice that's flagged at risk

Analysis — AI helps:

- Drafting specific, verifiable checks from a description of what the instruction was supposed to ensure
- Drafting the narrative from the checklist actually built

Drudgery — automated:

- Tallying how many practices are still holding
- Identifying which practices are at risk
- Exporting to xlsx in the house format
